By David Gluckman

Overview

Think Audi, and two things likely come to mind: technology and all-wheel drive. The Q4 e-tron electric crossover meets the first part of that brief pretty well, but only the more powerful 55 version gets a dual-motor, all-wheel-drive system, while the entry-level 45 makes do with a single rear motor and rear drive.

While the Q4 e-tron is sufficiently differentiated from the Volkswagen ID.4 that it shares its compact-SUV platform with, none of the Audi's specs are standouts in the segment. Its driving personality is best described as poised, but it's not as enjoyable to pilot as some of the more fun-loving EV SUVs in its class. Charging speed is mid-pack, as is the range you get from a full battery pack—EPA estimates of 258 miles for the more powerful 55 version and 288 for the 45. Indeed, Audi has created a small EV SUV that does everything well enough to not offend, but nothing that makes it a shining star.

Expert Tip: Audi's recently redesigned Q5 and high-performance SQ5 SUVs offer similar space but retain gas engines and are more fun to drive.

What's New for 2026?

Audi has simplified the Q4 lineup this year, dropping the top Prestige trim level and adding more content to what was the mid-range Premium Plus. The latter now comes with the Park Assist Plus self-parking feature, a 360-degree surround-view camera system, and a Sonos-branded sound system. A Vision package is now available on Q4 e-tron 55 models and includes matrix-design LED headlights, headlight washers, and a head-up display, while opting for the Black optic pack on the 55s now nets black exterior trim and Audi interlocking-ring badges.

C/D Expert Tip:

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

EV Motor, Power, and Performance

  • EV Motors: 282-hp single motor, 335-hp dual motor
  • Drivetrains: rear-wheel-drive, all-wheel-drive

The entry-level Q4 e-tron 45 comes with a single 282-hp electric motor that powers the rear wheels. We haven’t had a chance to drive the Q4 e-tron with this setup yet. With an electric motor powering each axle, the all-wheel-drive Q4 e-tron 55 and Q4 e-tron Sportback 55 models make 335 horsepower.

The Q4 e-tron's road manners are polite; the ride is smooth, and the Audi feels reasonably maneuverable thanks to a tight turning radius. Audi also recently made improvements to the handling, and we noticed steering that's slightly more accurate and cornering that is a touch more stable.

0–60-MPH Times

  • C/D 60-mph Test: 5.0 seconds (55)

In Comparison: The 355-hp base Porsche Macan EV ties the Q4 e-tron 55's 5.0-second 60-mph time.

    Towing and Payload Capacity

    • Max Towing: 2650 pounds

    The Q4 e-tron can't tow a whole lot, but at least it can tow. The 45 powertrain can handle 2200 pounds, while the 55 provides a bit more capacity (2650 pounds) and is likely to be easier to pull with. Just remember that EV range drops precipitously with a trailer attached.

    Range, Charging, and Battery Life

    • C/D Range Test: 220 miles (Sportback 55)
    • EPA EV Range: 258-288 miles

    The Q4 e-tron’s 77.0-kWh battery pack provides up to an EPA-rated 288 miles per charge when paired with the standard single-motor 45 powertrain, and up to 258 miles per charge in the all-wheel-drive Q4 e-tron 55. In our 75-mph real-world highway range test, the Q4 e-tron Sportback 55 achieved 220 miles.

    All models now support fast charging at up to 175 kW and, according to Audi, can be recharged from 10 to 80 percent in 28 minutes. This is slower than the class-leading Genesis GV60, which is capable of charging to the same level in just 18 minutes, according to Genesis. In our testing, the Q4 charged from 10 percent to 90 percent in 36 minutes.

    Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe

    • C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel-Economy Test: 95 MPGe (Sportback 55)
    • EPA City Ratings: 107-125 MPGe
    • EPA Highway Ratings: 92-104 MPGe

    The EPA hasn’t released any fuel-economy information for the 2026 Q4 e-tron yet, but the 2025 model earned ratings of 107-125 MPGe city, 92-104 MPGe highway, and 100-115 MPGe combined. With no changes to the lineup for 2026, we don't expect its fuel economy numbers to change.

    MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV vehicle fuel efficiency. For more information about the Q4 e-tron's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

    Interior, Comfort, and Cargo

    First Row: Like other Audi models, the Q4 e-tron's cabin is a technological showcase for the brand's latest and greatest gadgets. It incorporates a few unique features, including a squared-off steering wheel with touch-sensitive controls. Both the Q4 e-tron and the Q4 e-tron Sportback offer seating for five. We think those seats could use a bit more cushioning.

    Second Row: The interior passenger space is about the same as in the slightly larger, gas-powered Q5. Rear legroom is adequate if not generous. Opting for the Sportback cuts down slightly on rear headroom, so keep that in mind if you plan to ferry six-footers often.

    Cargo Capacity: We fit eight carry-on suitcases behind the Q4 e-tron's rear seat and 22 in total with the seat backs folded.

    View Photos

    Infotainment and Connectivity

    • Infotainment: 11.6-inch touchscreen
    • Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto functionality
    • Audio System: 10-speaker stereo (standard), 19-speaker Sonos stereo (optional)

    The Q4 e-tron has the latest version of Audi’s MMI system. A 10.3-inch digital gauge display is standard, and a large 11.6-inch infotainment touchscreen is angled toward the driver for easier access to its various menus and features. Audi also offers a head-up display with an augmented reality feature that can project information such as navigation instructions or driver-assistance warnings in the driver's line of sight.

    Safety and Driver-Assistance Features

    Overall Safety Rating (NHTSA)

    View Crash Test Results

    The Q4 e-tron models are stocked with plenty of driver-assistance technology features, such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and automated emergency braking.

    • Standard Safety Features: forward-collision warning and automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert, adaptive cruise control with a lane-centering feature

    For information about the Q4 e-tron's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

    Warranty and Maintenance Coverage

    The Audi Q4 e-tron and Q4 e-tron Sportback offer the same limited and powertrain warranty as the larger Q8 e-tron SUV.

    • Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
    • Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
    • Electric Components Warranty: eight years or 100,000 miles
    • Complimentary Maintenance: three years or 30,000 miles
